title: Cyclotron orbit (magnetized)
description: 1D3V electrons in a uniform Bz = 1 with a perpendicular drift. The Boris pusher rotates v_⊥ at the cyclotron frequency ω_c = |q/m| B while the weak self-consistent Ex stays small. Watch velocityY oscillate and total energy stay bounded.
lookFor: Mean v_y oscillating at about the cyclotron period 2π
Phase-space motion with a rotating perpendicular velocity
Field energy remaining small (ω_p ≪ ω_c)
Total energy approximately conserved (B does no work)

title: 3D Larmor helix
description: Electrons in B_z = 1 with parallel drift (v_x, v_z) and a perpendicular kick (v_y). Each particle traces a **helical Larmor orbit** while the cloud stays nearly neutral — weak ω_p = 0.06 keeps E small. Dense frame output (period 1) for smooth 3D playback: enable auto-rotate and watch the spring-like particle paths wrap the domain.
lookFor: Helical trajectories in the rotatable 3D particle view
Cyclotron gyration in the x–y plane plus drift along x and z
Perpendicular kinetic energy oscillating at ω_c ≈ 1
Total energy flat (external B does no work)

title: 3D cyclotron storm
description: A **1024-particle** warm electron cloud in strong B_z = 1.25. Every particle gyrates at a slightly different phase; together they form a spinning, turbulent-looking **cyclotron storm** in the 3D view. Great for showcasing Boris stability with thermal spread (v_th = 0.18) and fast timestep (Δt = 0.06).
lookFor: Dense, rapidly rotating 3D particle cloud
Broad perpendicular velocity spread from thermal gyration
Field energy tiny compared with kinetic (ω_p = 0.04)
Smooth animation with one frame per step

title: 3D oblique B field
description: Tilted uniform field **B = (0.35, 0.35, 0.85)** breaks symmetry: Larmor circles no longer lie in the x–y plane. Rotate the 3D view to see the **inclined gyration axis** and how a warm cloud (v_th = 0.12) fills a tilted torus-like volume.
lookFor: Gyration axis tilted away from z in the 3D scatter view
Perpendicular motion split across all three velocity components
Different apparent orbit shapes from different camera angles
Energy budget dominated by gyrational kinetic energy

title: 3D cross-field gyration (B_x)
description: Field along **x** instead of z: **B = (1, 0, 0)**. Perpendicular drifts in y and z produce **pinwheel motion in the y–z plane** as particles slide along x. A striking change of perspective from the usual textbook B_z setup.
lookFor: Circular motion primarily in the y–z plane (3D view)
Gyration frequency set by |B| = 1
Thermal spread smearing individual orbit radii
Auto-rotate highlights the transverse plane of gyration

title: 3D magnetized two-stream
description: Classic **counter-streaming beams** (v_x = ±1) plus **B_z = 0.75**. Gyroradius r_L ≈ v/ω_c modulates the instability: beams filament and wrap into **spiraling vortex-like structures** in 3D instead of flat 1D phase-space rolls. Two species colors in the scatter view.
lookFor: Two colored beam populations mixing in 3D
Gyro-orbit scale visible before nonlinear saturation
Electrostatic energy growth from the two-stream drive
Instability + magnetization interplay (ω_p/ω_c ≈ 0.47)

title: Magnetized plasma wave
description: Standing-wave density perturbation (sin, mode k = 1) in a warm magnetized plasma: **B_z = 1**, **ω_p = 0.25**, perpendicular drift v_y = 0.4. Watch **E(x) breathe** at the plasma frequency while every particle simultaneously **gyrates** at ω_c — two oscillations superposed in the energy budget.
lookFor: E(x) oscillation plus cyclotron modulation in phase space
Competition between ω_p and ω_c in the Energy tab
Perpendicular velocity rotating at ω_c = 1
Total energy approximately conserved

title: Magnetized two-stream (1D3V)
description: Two cold beams at **v_x = ±1** with **B_z = 0.7** and small perpendicular drifts (v_y = ±0.2). The instability still drives field growth, but phase space shows **rotating beamlets** instead of simple horizontal stripes — magnetization wraps the classic two-stream picture.
lookFor: Phase-space filaments curved by cyclotron motion
Field energy rise from two-stream instability
Perpendicular velocity components in exported frames (velocityY)
ω_c ≈ 0.7, ω_p ≈ 0.5 — comparable magnetization

title: E×B drift (1D3V)
description: Small sin perturbation seeds a self-consistent **E_x(x)** while **B_z = 1** pins cyclotron motion. Electrons simultaneously **gyrate** and **drift in y** with speed v_E ≈ E/B from the wave field — the textbook **E×B** pattern in a fully kinetic PIC setup (weak ω_p = 0.15).
lookFor: Slow net drift in y superposed on fast cyclotron wobble
E(x) pattern sloshing while particles drift across it
Perpendicular kinetic energy >> field energy
Export velocityY in frame CSV to see drift + gyration

title: Two-stream vortex formation
description: Strong counter-streaming beams (v = ±1.2, amplitude 0.012) on a 64-cell grid with dense frame output. Watch phase space roll into classic trapping vortices as electrostatic energy saturates. Auto-plays with interpolated frames for smooth motion.
lookFor: Phase-space vortices / holes forming after linear growth
Rapid rise then saturation of field energy
Smooth animation (~300 keyframes with interpolation)
Best showcase of nonlinear two-stream dynamics

title: Two-stream (quick)
description: Two cold electron beams stream past each other with a tiny k = 1 density perturbation. The counter-streaming setup is the classic testbed for the two-stream instability: electrostatic energy grows exponentially, then saturates as particles trap in the wave.
lookFor: Phase space: two separated beams that broaden and filament over time
Electrostatic energy rises sharply after an initial quiet period
Kinetic energy falls as particles exchange energy with the field
Fast run (~300 particles, coarse 32-cell grid)

title: Two-stream (strong drive)
description: Same two-beam geometry as the quick case, but with a larger initial perturbation (amplitude 0.008). The instability kicks in sooner and field growth is easier to see in the first half of the run.
lookFor: Earlier and steeper rise in electrostatic energy than the quick case
Stronger field amplitudes in the E(x) animation
More rapid beam mixing in phase space
Good choice if you want visible dynamics without waiting long

title: Two-stream (warm beams)
description: Counter-propagating beams with finite temperature (v_th = 0.12). Thermal spread fills out phase space around each beam while the two-stream mode still grows. Compare with the cold cases to see how temperature changes the instability pathway.
lookFor: Phase-space clouds around ±drift velocity instead of thin lines
Instability still develops, but with more diffuse trapping structures
Finer 64-cell grid resolves slightly more spatial structure
Total energy should stay approximately conserved

title: Plasma oscillation (smooth)
description: Cold electron plasma oscillation with dense frames (period 2) so the Animation tab shows a fluid ω ≈ ω_p cycle in phase space and E(x). Ideal for checking that playback interpolation looks natural.
lookFor: Regular breathing of E(x) and electrostatic energy
Particles bunch and unbunch near v = 0
Smooth continuous motion between saved frames
Energy nearly conserved over many oscillation periods

title: Electron plasma oscillation
description: Single cold electron species with a small standing-wave perturbation. In the absence of beams or thermal Landau damping, the system supports an undamped electron plasma oscillation at ω ≈ ω_p. A short, lightweight run ideal for watching basic wave physics.
lookFor: Regular oscillation of E(x) and electrostatic energy
Phase space stays near v = 0 with modest spatial bunching
|E_k| envelope roughly constant after initial transients
Short run — good first demo to try

title: Landau damping (smooth)
description: Warm standing wave with dense frame sampling so the |E_k| decay and phase-space filamentation animate smoothly. Compare with Cold plasma (quick) to isolate physical Landau damping from numerical artifacts.
lookFor: Smooth |E_k| envelope decay on a log scale
E(x) antinodes shrink while nodes stay fixed
Phase-space filaments near the resonant velocity
ESE late/early ratio well below 1

title: Landau damping (quick)
description: A warm (v_th = 0.4) electron plasma on a periodic domain is given a small standing-wave density perturbation (sin shift, mode k = 1). Resonant particles near the wave phase velocity absorb field energy, so the |E_k| envelope decays even though the spatial cos(kx) pattern is preserved.
lookFor: E(x) antinode amplitude shrinks while nodes stay fixed
|E_k| plot shows log-scale decay over the run
ESE late/early ratio well below 1 in the analysis summary
Compare with Cold plasma (quick) to isolate physical damping

title: Cold plasma wave (quick)
description: Identical setup to Landau quick except v_th = 0. Without a velocity tail at the resonant speed, there is no Landau mechanism — the launched standing wave should oscillate without sustained envelope decay. Use this as the control when interpreting warm Landau results.
lookFor: |E_k| amplitude stays near its initial level
ESE late/early ratio close to 1 (typically 0.9–1.2)
E(x) pattern oscillates but does not systematically decay
Pair with Landau quick to see warm-vs-cold contrast

title: Landau damping (mode 2)
description: Warm standing wave with spatial mode m = 2 (k = 2 on a 2π domain). Higher-k waves have shorter wavelength and often damp faster in PIC, so |E_k| decay should be more pronounced than the k = 1 Landau quick case.
lookFor: E(x) shows two antinodes per domain length
Fourier panel tracks mode m = 2 amplitude
Typically faster |E_k| decay than k = 1 warm case
Standing-wave nodes remain at fixed positions

title: Drifting warm beam
description: One warm electron beam (drift v = 0.8, v_th = 0.25) with a standing-wave perturbation. The drifting Maxwellian interacts with the self-consistent field, producing shear and mixing in phase space distinct from the two-stream or pure Landau cases.
lookFor: Phase-space cloud centered near the drift velocity
E(x) and |E_k| evolve with both oscillation and beam spreading
Energy budget: kinetic energy dominates; field energy is a small fraction
Useful for exploring wave–particle motion beyond textbook benchmarks

title: 3D two-stream
description: Counter-streaming electron beams in 3D on an 8³ grid. Use the rotatable 3D particle view (auto-rotate on by default) to watch the two populations mix. Dense frames plus interpolation keep the motion smooth.
lookFor: Two colored populations in the 3D scatter view
Drag or auto-rotate to inspect filamentation
Field energy growth as the instability develops
2D slices tab for XY/XZ/YZ projections

title: 3D plasma breathing
description: Longer 3D cold-plasma oscillation (120 steps, frame period 2) so the cloud visibly breathes in the rotatable view. Turn on auto-rotate and Play for a cinematic loop.
lookFor: 3D density modulation oscillating in time
Smooth interpolated particle motion
Ex mid-plane slice tracking ω_p
Auto-rotate + loop for a continuous presentation

title: 3D plasma oscillation (quick)
description: Single-species 3D electrostatic plasma oscillation on an 8³ grid with 512 particles. The desktop GUI shows an interactive rotatable 3D particle view (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom), optional 2D slice projections, and a mid-plane Ex slice.
lookFor: 3D particles tab: drag to rotate the cloud, scroll to zoom
Ghost trails show motion between saved frames
Ex mid-plane slice oscillates with the plasma frequency
2D slices tab for XY/XZ/YZ projections

title: Ion–electron oscillation
description: Cold electrons plus light ions (q/m = +0.05, ω_p,i ≪ ω_p,e). Electrons oscillate rapidly while ions provide a slower neutralizing background — useful for discussing multi-species electrostatic response.
lookFor: Two species in phase space with different velocity scales
Field energy oscillates with an electron-dominated period
Ions barely move compared with electrons
Run from the demo file (not the simplified form) to preserve ion parameters

title: Landau damping (full)
description: Validation-resolution warm Landau case: 8000 particles and a 256-cell grid, matching inputFiles/validation/landauDamping.json. Slower but produces clean |E_k| decay and the same physics cited in docs/validation.md.
lookFor: Clear |E_k| end/start ratio ≈ 0.2–0.3 (strong damping)
Smooth E(x) snapshots with well-resolved nodes and antinodes
ESE late/early ratio typically ≈ 0.8
Expect longer run time — watch the progress bar

title: Two-stream (full)
description: Full validation two-stream parameters (500 particles per beam, 500 steps, 32-cell grid), matching inputFiles/validation/twoStreamInstability.json. Runs longer than the quick variant and reaches a more developed nonlinear stage.
lookFor: Extended growth and saturation of electrostatic energy
Strong phase-space filamentation and vortex-like structures
Peak ESE many times the initial perturbation level
Good for portfolio screenshots; moderate run time
